title: IPv6 basics
summary: 128-bit addresses, how to shorten them, the main types, and what replaces ARP, DHCP and NAT.

steps.title: 128 bits in hex
body: An IPv6 address is 128 bits, written as 8 groups of 4 hex digits:
Shortening rules: drop **leading zeros** in each group, and replace **one** run of all-zero groups with `::` (never twice, or it'd be ambiguous).
A LAN is almost always a **/64**: 64 bits of network, 64 of interface ID.

steps.prompt: `IPAddress` prints IPv6 in canonical short form. What does this print?
steps.explain: Leading zeros go, and the longest zero run becomes `::`.

steps.prompt: Match each address to its type.
pairs: Multicast: all nodes on the link

steps.prompt: Which is **not** a valid IPv6 address?
steps.explain: Two `::` would make it impossible to tell how many zero groups each one stands for.

steps.title: What changes from IPv4
body: - **No NAT needed**: there are enough addresses for every device to be globally unique. Firewalls still decide what's reachable.
- **No broadcast**: multicast instead. **NDP** (neighbor discovery, over ICMPv6) replaces ARP.
- **SLAAC**: hosts can build their own address from the router's advertised /64 prefix; DHCPv6 is optional.
- Blocking all ICMPv6 breaks IPv6: NDP and path MTU discovery depend on it.

steps.prompt: Match each IPv4 mechanism to its IPv6 counterpart.

steps.explain: Two zero runs of equal length: compress the **first** one (RFC 5952).

steps.title: Expand an address
prompt: Write `string Expand(string address)` returning all 8 groups, 4 lowercase hex digits each: `"2001:db8::1"` gives
`"2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001"`. Handle `::` at the start, middle or end, and `::` alone. Don't use `IPAddress`.
solution: var left = halves[0].Length > 0 ? halves[0].Split(':').ToList() : new List<string>();
var right = halves.Length > 1 && halves[1].Length > 0 ? halves[1].Split(':').ToList() : new List<string>();
var groups = halves.Length > 1 ? left.Concat(Enumerable.Repeat("0", 8 - left.Count - right.Count)).Concat(right) : left;
hints: Split on `::` into a left and right half; split each half on `:`.
Insert `8 - left - right` zero groups between them.

steps.title: Compress an address
prompt: Write `string Compress(string full)` producing the canonical form from 8 full groups: drop leading zeros (a group of zeros becomes `0`),
then replace the **longest** run of two or more zero groups with `::` (the first run on a tie). Don't use `IPAddress`.
solution: var g = full.Split(':').Select(x => x.TrimStart('0')).Select(x => x == "" ? "0" : x.ToLowerInvariant()).ToArray();
if (j - i > bestLen) { bestStart = i; bestLen = j - i; }
return string.Join(":", g[..bestStart]) + "::" + string.Join(":", g[(bestStart + bestLen)..]);
hints: First normalise every group with `TrimStart('0')` (empty becomes `0`).
Scan for the longest run of `0` groups, length at least 2.
